donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 213)
votes.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision".
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that partly let California tighten emissions rules for commercial harbor boats, including fishing boats. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 210)
votes.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision".
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that let California tighten emissions rules for ocean-going ships while they are docked. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (H R 2140)
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes Environmental Protection Agency grants through fiscal year 2029 to replace old diesel engines or add pollution controls. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act (H R 2860)
votes.bill_title: Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill revises and reauthorizes for seven years the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative and its Northwest Straits Advisory Commission. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act (H R 1346)
votes.bill_title: To amend the Clean Air Act with respect to the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under that Act, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill amends the Clean Air Act to address the limitations on Reid Vapor Pressure (a measure of gasoline's volatility) that are placed on gasoline during the summer ozone season. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act (H R 1346)
votes.bill_title: To amend the Clean Air Act with respect to the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under that Act, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: H.R. 1346 amends the Clean Air Act to address the limitations on Reid Vapor Pressure (a measure of gasoline's volatility) that are placed on gasoline during the summer ozone season. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — FIRE Act (H R 6387)
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies the definition of exceptional events under the Clean Air Act and requires the Environmental Protection Agency to revise its regulations regarding exceptional events or actions to mitigate wildfire risk. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — FIRE Act (H R 6387)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6387 (FIRE Act) modifies the definition of exceptional events under the Clean Air Act and requires the Environmental Protection Agency to revise its regulations regarding exceptional events or actions to mitigate wildfire risk. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — RED Tape Act (H R 6398)
votes.plain_language: This bill removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on newly authorized federal construction projects and other major federal agency actions that already require review under the National Environmental Policy Act and proposed federal regulations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — RED Tape Act (H R 6398)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6398 (RED Tape Act) removes the requirement under the Clean Air Act that the Environmental Protection Agency review and comment on newly authorized federal construction projects and other major federal agency actions that already require review under the National Environmental Policy Act and proposed federal regulations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — FENCES Act (H R 6409)
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies standards under the Clean Air Act to exempt states from penalties for emissions outside of the state’s control. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — FENCES Act (H R 6409)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6409 (FENCES Act) modifies standards under the Clean Air Act to exempt states from penalties for emissions outside of the state’s control. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — American Water Stewardship Act (H R 6422)
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes several water quality protection and restoration programs of the Environmental Protection Agency and makes related requirements. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Secure America Act (S 2)
votes.plain_language: This bill provides $70 billion in funding to the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through FY2029 for immigration enforcement, border security, and related activities. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Commit — Secure America Act (S 2)
votes.plain_language: S. 2, the Secure America Act, provides $70 billion to the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through FY2029 for immigration enforcement, border security, and related activities, under budget reconciliation procedures. A motion to commit, like a motion to recommit, is the minority's last formal chance to send the bill to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it to committee; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution, as Amended — Expressing the support of the House of Representatives for the Department of Homeland Security (H RES 1128)
votes.bill_title: Expressing the support of the House of Representatives for the Department of Homeland Security.
votes.plain_language: This resolution recognizes the importance of fully funding the Department of Homeland Security. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — BOWOW Act (H R 4638)
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes that a non-U.S. national convicted of, or who admits to having committed, an offense related to harming animals used in law enforcement is inadmissible and deportable. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Deporting Fraudsters Act (H R 1958)
votes.plain_language: This bill makes certain acts related to public benefits fraud grounds for (1) barring a non-U.S. national from admission into the United States, or (2) deporting the individual. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Relating to a national emergency by the President on February 1, 2025 (H J RES 72)
votes.bill_title: Relating to a national emergency by the President on February 1, 2025.
votes.plain_language: The official title of H.J.Res. 72 is “Relating to a national emergency by the President on February 1, 2025.” No official summary was available. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
